editorial.headline: The Business of Making the Right Connection
editorial.standfirst: This activity formalises the service of bringing clients and providers together—and remains open to foreign investment nationally and for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is a business-support intermediation service for work not otherwise specified. Its operating unit makes the introduction: it brings a client together with a service provider under a fee or contract. That deceptively simple function is the centre of gravity. The business is not defined by creating the underlying service; it is defined by arranging the connection through which that service can be taken up. The description deliberately places it in the supporting layer of business, built around the match between demand and provision.

The method is deliberately broad. It can operate through a digital platform or through nondigital channels, including face-to-face contact, door-to-door work, telephone and correspondence. Payment may come from the client or the service provider, in the form of a fee or commission. Intermediation income may also include other sources, such as advertising income. The scope expressly includes reservations and ticket sales for theatre, sports and other entertainment events. A digital interface is therefore one possible route, not the condition that defines the activity.

It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The breadth is significant because the record does not reserve the activity for one size of enterprise. At every listed scale, the commercial identity remains the same: connecting clients and service providers under the agreed commercial basis of a fee or contract. For founders, the practical reading is one of scope: the record places every listed scale within the available range without changing the essential intermediary role.

Nationally, this activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign founder, the decisive Bali point is clear: it is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali’s status is OK or higher risk; at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That places it outside a moratorium that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali. The distinction matters: the national ceiling records national openness, while the Bali position answers whether that opening is stopped by the local moratorium. On this record, it is not.
editorial.pullQuote: The business is defined by arranging the connection through which a service can be taken up.
